#

144A

A private bond placement sold only to qualified institutional buyers.

Defined in: W02

The "$600B question"

Sequoia's 2024 test of how much end-customer revenue AI needs to justify GPU spending. The Atlas update (W11) puts it at ~$1.6T on Sequoia's method and ~$600B a year on a depreciation basis.

Defined in: W00

800 V DC (HVDC)

NVIDIA-led architecture distributing high-voltage DC to racks from 2027.

Defined in: W04

A

A16 / A14

TSMC's 1.6nm-class and 1.4nm-class nodes (A = ångström).

Defined in: W06

A2A (Agent2Agent)

Google-originated protocol for agents to communicate with each other.

Defined in: W10

ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film)

Insulating film used to build the fine-wiring layers of chip package substrates.

Defined in: W06

ABS / CMBS / SASB

Asset-backed securities / commercial mortgage-backed securities / single-asset single-borrower CMBS: bonds repaid from pooled lease payments, such as data-center rents. They let developers refinance stabilized buildings at bond-market rates.

Defined in: W02W04merged ×2

Absorption (net)

Change in occupied or committed capacity over a period. CBRE measures leased colo in primary markets. JLL includes self-build and frontier markets.

Defined in: W04

Accelerator

Any chip specialized for AI math (GPU, TPU, NPU, LPU, XPU).

Defined in: W05

ACIE

NVIDIA's reporting sub-market "AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise" (from FY27): its non-hyperscale data-center customers, such as neoclouds, sovereign projects, labs and enterprises.

Defined in: W05W07merged ×2

ACV (annual contract value)

Yearly value of a signed contract; ServiceNow reports AI ACV.

Defined in: W10

Advanced packaging

Joining several dies (logic, memory) in one package with very dense interconnects (2.5D side by side, 3D stacked).

Defined in: W06

AEC (active electrical cable)

Copper cable with retimer/DSP chips in the connectors; reaches ~5–7 m at 100–200G/lane.

Defined in: W07

Aeroderivative

A jet-engine-derived gas turbine (e.g. LM2500/LM6000). Fast to deploy, less efficient, used on-site.

Defined in: W03

Agent

An AI system that is given a goal and pursues it over many steps on its own: it plans, calls tools (browser, terminal, APIs) and iterates with little human input (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor's agent). An agent task uses roughly 4–15× more tokens than a chat.

Defined in: W00W09W10merged ×3

Agentic Work Unit (AWU)

Salesforce's usage metric for agent actions (3.2B in Q2 FY27).

Defined in: W10

AGI clause

A contract term (Microsoft–OpenAI) that changes rights and revenue share once "artificial general intelligence" is declared and verified by an expert panel.

Defined in: W09

AI build-out

The global investment program in data centers, chips, networking and power to train and run AI models.

Defined in: W00

AI factory

NVIDIA's term for a data center built mainly to produce tokens (training or inference).

Defined in: W04

AI-attributable

The share of a multi-business company's revenue or profit caused by AI demand.

Defined in: W11

AI-induced shortage rent

Profit earned from non-AI buyers because AI demand created the shortage (e.g. PC and phone DRAM in 2026).

Defined in: W11

ARR / run-rate

Annual recurring revenue: the latest month's revenue × 12 (or week × 52, quarter × 4). For usage-based AI businesses it is not contracted revenue, it overstates calendar-year revenue when growth is fast, and it can fall as quickly as it rose.

Defined in: W00W08W09W10W11merged ×5

ASIC / XPU

Application-specific integrated circuit: a custom AI accelerator designed for one customer's workloads, such as Google's TPU, Amazon's Trainium or Meta's MTIA. Broadcom calls these chips "XPUs".

Defined in: W00W05W07merged ×3

ASP

Average selling price.

Defined in: W05

ATC (around-the-clock)

A flat 24/7 power block, the typical hyperscaler "firm" product.

Defined in: W03

ATE

Automated test equipment (Advantest, Teradyne).

Defined in: W06

ATM (at-the-market) offering

Selling new shares gradually into the market at prevailing prices through brokers, rather than in one large deal.

Defined in: W01W02merged ×2

B

Backside power (Super Power Rail, PowerVia)

Routing power through the back of the wafer, freeing the front for signals.

Defined in: W06

Backstop

A promise to buy unused capacity (e.g. Nvidia's $6.3B CoreWeave backstop).

Defined in: W02

Base die

The bottom die of an HBM stack; since HBM4 it is made on a logic process (often by TSMC).

Defined in: W06

Base model

The output of pre-training, before instruction tuning.

Defined in: W09

BBU

Battery backup unit in the rack.

Defined in: W07

BDC

Business development company. A US vehicle, often sold to retail investors, that makes private loans.

Defined in: W02

BESS

Battery energy storage system.

Defined in: W03

BF16 / FP8 / FP4 / NVFP4 / MXFP4

Number formats with 16, 8 or 4 bits. NVFP4 is NVIDIA's 4-bit format with fine-grained scaling. MXFP4 is the OCP-standard equivalent.

Defined in: W05

Book-to-bill

Orders received ÷ revenue billed in the same period. Above 1 means the backlog is growing.

Defined in: W04

BRA (Base Residual Auction)

PJM's main capacity auction, held ~3 years (lately less) before the delivery year.

Defined in: W03

Bridge loan

A short-term loan (e.g. 1 year) to be refinanced later with bonds or asset sales.

Defined in: W02

BTM (behind-the-meter)

Generation on the customer's side of the utility meter, such as on-site gas turbines or fuel cells, rather than power taken from the grid. It avoids some grid charges and queues; FERC is now restricting "netting" of such load.

Defined in: W00W03merged ×2

Busway

Overhead copper or aluminum bars carrying power to racks, replacing cable.

Defined in: W04

BYOG

"bring your own generation". A large load arrives with new supply to avoid burdening the grid.

Defined in: W03

BYOH (bring your own hardware)

The customer buys the GPUs and the cloud operates them (Oracle).

Defined in: W01

C

Cap rate

Stabilized NOI ÷ asset value; a lower cap rate means a higher valuation.

Defined in: W04

Capacity factor / load factor

Actual output (or consumption) ÷ maximum possible over a period.

Defined in: W03

Capacity market

An auction (in PJM, the Base Residual Auction) in which utilities pay power plants, in $/MW-day, to be available to generate or curtail at peak times. It is paid separately from energy ($/MWh). AI load has driven PJM's price up more than 11×.

Defined in: W00W03merged ×2

Capex (capital expenditure)

Spending on long-lasting assets such as servers and buildings. It is recorded as an asset and depreciated over the years the asset is used, rather than expensed at once.

Defined in: W00W01merged ×2

Cash capex / purchases of PP&E

Capex actually paid in cash in the period.

Defined in: W01

CCGT

Combined-cycle gas turbine. A gas turbine plus a steam turbine using waste heat; ~60%+ efficient; the grid's baseload gas workhorse.

Defined in: W03

CDS (credit default swap)

Insurance against a borrower's default. Its price, a spread in basis points a year, is a live gauge of how risky the market thinks the borrower is.

Defined in: W02W08merged ×2

CDU (coolant distribution unit)

The pump and heat exchanger that link a rack's liquid-cooling loop to the facility water loop. A core piece of liquid cooling.

Defined in: W04W07merged ×2

Chip-backed SPV

A special-purpose vehicle that buys accelerators and leases them to a lab, with debt secured on the chips and the lease (e.g. Anthropic's ~$35B Apollo/Blackstone SPV, where Broadcom guarantees the chips' residual value).

Defined in: W02

CHIPS Act

The 2022 US law with US$39 bn of manufacturing incentives and a 25% (now 35%) investment tax credit.

Defined in: W06

Circular (vendor) financing

A supplier invests in, lends to, or guarantees a customer, and the customer spends that money buying from the supplier (Nvidia → OpenAI, AMD → Anthropic, Amazon → Anthropic). It supports demand but ties the supplier's revenue to the customer's ability to raise money.

Defined in: W00W02W08W09W11merged ×5

Clos / fat tree

Multi-tier switch topology that gives any-to-any bandwidth.

Defined in: W07

ClusterMAX

SemiAnalysis's rating of GPU clouds (Platinum → Bronze).

Defined in: W08

Co-location

A data center physically sited at a power plant, taking power directly.

Defined in: W03

Colocation / wholesale lease

Renting space and power in someone else's data center, priced per kW per month.

Defined in: W00

Computer use

A model operating a graphical interface (screenshots, clicks, typing).

Defined in: W10

Containment / resolution rate

Share of customer conversations an agent completes without a human.

Defined in: W10

Context window

The amount of text (tokens) a model can consider at once. Agents re-send it every step.

Defined in: W10

Contracted power (neocloud)

MW or GW of data-center capacity a GPU cloud has secured under signed leases or ownership, whether or not it is yet energized ("active power"). CoreWeave reports both.

Defined in: W04

Contracted vs active power

MW signed under lease vs MW energized and hosting billing GPUs.

Defined in: W08

Convertible note

A bond that can convert into shares. It has a low coupon because it includes an equity option.

Defined in: W02

Copilot

An AI assistant embedded in an existing workflow that suggests while a human decides (GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot). The step before an agent.

Defined in: W00W10merged ×2

CoPoS

Chip-on-Panel-on-Substrate, TSMC's panel-based successor to CoWoS.

Defined in: W06

Cost of revenue (CoR) / COGS

For labs, mainly inference compute plus hosting, revenue share and payment fees.

Defined in: W09

CoWoS (-S / -L / -R)

Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate: TSMC's 2.5D advanced packaging, which places GPU logic dies and HBM side by side on a silicon interposer (-S), local silicon bridges (-L, for larger multi-die packages) or a redistribution-layer interposer (-R). It was the key bottleneck in 2023–24.

Defined in: W00W05W06merged ×3

CPO (co-packaged optics)

Optical engines in the same package as the switch/processor ASIC.

Defined in: W07

Critical IT load (MW IT)

Megawatts available to IT equipment, excluding cooling overhead. Gross (utility) MW is higher by the PUE and redundancy overhead.

Defined in: W04W08merged ×2

CSP

Cloud service provider (a hyperscaler).

Defined in: W06

CUDA

NVIDIA's programming platform for its GPUs (2006), and the core of its software moat.

Defined in: W05

CW laser

Continuous-wave laser, used with silicon-photonic modulators.

Defined in: W07

D

D&A

Depreciation (tangible assets) and amortisation (intangibles), non-cash expenses.

Defined in: W01

Data center

A building housing computers, with its own electrical, cooling and network infrastructure.

Defined in: W00

DCI

Data-center interconnect (links between sites).

Defined in: W07

DDTL (delayed-draw term loan)

A loan drawn in stages as the assets it finances (GPUs) are delivered, secured by those GPUs and the customer contracts they serve. CoreWeave's main funding tool.

Defined in: W02W08merged ×2

Decode / prefill

The two phases of LLM inference: token generation (memory-bound) and prompt processing (compute-bound).

Defined in: W05

Dense vs sparse FLOPS

Sparse ratings assume 2:4 structured sparsity and are 2× dense.

Defined in: W05

Depreciation / useful life

Spreading an asset's cost over the years it is used. Servers are depreciated over about 5–6 years and buildings over 15–25. The useful life is the central accounting judgement for GPU fleets: longer lives mean lower annual depreciation and higher reported profit today.

Defined in: W00W01W08merged ×3

Depreciation wall

The rising annual depreciation charge that follows a capex surge, as short-lived IT assets enter service.

Defined in: W11

Depreciation-based requirement

The revenue needed for capex to earn its cost of capital: depreciation + opex + return, grossed up for downstream margins.

Defined in: W11

Direct-to-chip (DLC)

Liquid-cooled cold plates on processors.

Defined in: W04

Disaggregated inference

Running prefill and decode on different hardware pools.

Defined in: W05

Distillation

Training a smaller or cheaper model on the outputs of a stronger model.

Defined in: W09

DPU / SuperNIC

Smart network card (BlueField, ConnectX-8/9).

Defined in: W07

DRAM / NAND

The two main memory types: DRAM (working memory) and NAND (flash storage, SSDs).

Defined in: W00

Dry cooler / air-cooled chiller

Rejects heat to outside air without evaporating water.

Defined in: W04

DSCR (debt-service coverage ratio)

Cash available for debt service ÷ required payments. 1.12× means 12% headroom.

Defined in: W02

DSO

Days sales outstanding, how long customers take to pay.

Defined in: W05

DSP (in optics)

Chip that cleans and encodes the high-speed signal (PAM4) inside a transceiver.

Defined in: W07

E

EDA

Electronic design automation, the software used to design chips.

Defined in: W06

ELCC

Effective load-carrying capability. How much a resource counts toward reliability (e.g. solar counts little at winter peaks).

Defined in: W03

Elo (LMArena)

A relative-preference rating derived from head-to-head human votes.

Defined in: W09

EMIB / EMIB-T

Intel's Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge: small silicon bridges buried in the package substrate that link dies. EMIB-T adds through-silicon vias and is Intel's alternative to CoWoS.

Defined in: W05W06merged ×2

EML

Electro-absorption modulated laser; the classic 100G/200G-per-lane laser, made on InP.

Defined in: W07

End-customer AI money

Consumer, enterprise and advertiser spending on AI products, AI infrastructure services and AI-driven ads, net of intermediate purchases (e.g. an app buying API tokens).

Defined in: W11

ERCOT

The Texas grid operator (mostly outside FERC jurisdiction). Batch Zero: its 2026 cluster-study process for large loads.

Defined in: W03

ESA

Electric service agreement between a utility and a customer.

Defined in: W03

ESUN

Ethernet for Scale-Up Networking (OCP workstream led by Meta and Microsoft).

Defined in: W07

EUV / DUV / High-NA EUV

Lithography generations. Deep-UV (193nm) prints older layers; extreme-UV (13.5nm) prints the finest features; High-NA EUV uses a 0.55 numerical aperture for finer still. ASML is the only maker of EUV machines.

Defined in: W00W06merged ×2

Exaflop (EF)

10¹⁸ FLOPS.

Defined in: W05

F

FCF (free cash flow)

Operating cash flow minus capex (sometimes also minus finance-lease principal). It turned negative at Alphabet (Q2 2026), Amazon (trailing twelve months) and Oracle as AI capex surged.

Defined in: W00W01W02merged ×3

FERC

Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. Regulates wholesale markets and interstate transmission.

Defined in: W03

Finance lease

A lease that transfers most of an asset's economic life. Booked like a debt-financed purchase; Microsoft and Meta include it in the capex they discuss.

Defined in: W01

FLAP-D

Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, Dublin, Europe's legacy data-center hubs.

Defined in: W03

FLOP / FLOPS

A floating-point operation / floating-point operations per second: the unit of AI arithmetic. Frontier training runs use roughly 10^26–10^27 FLOP.

Defined in: W05W09merged ×2

Flow-of-funds

A cash map of who pays whom in a period, including capital spending and financing, not just profits.

Defined in: W11

Force majeure

A contract clause excusing performance when extraordinary events prevent it.

Defined in: W01

Foundry

A company that manufactures chips designed by others. TSMC is the dominant one.

Defined in: W00W06merged ×2

Frontier market

A region with little prior DC development, e.g., West Texas, Louisiana, North Dakota (JLL).

Defined in: W04

Frontier model

Among the most capable models available at a point in time.

Defined in: W09

Front-of-meter

Supply delivered via the grid (paying transmission charges), as opposed to BTM.

Defined in: W03

G

GAA / nanosheet

Gate-all-around transistors, where the gate wraps the channel on all sides (TSMC N2, Intel 18A, Samsung SF2).

Defined in: W06

GPU (graphics processing unit)

A chip with thousands of parallel arithmetic units; Nvidia's GPUs are the workhorse of AI.

Defined in: W00

GPU-hour

One accelerator for one hour; the basic unit of GPU rental pricing.

Defined in: W08

Gross margin

(Revenue − cost of goods sold) ÷ revenue. For AI apps and labs, cost of goods is mostly tokens and inference compute, so gross margins sit well below classic software's.

Defined in: W06W10merged ×2

GW / MW

Gigawatt / megawatt of power; AI capacity and compute deals are now counted in GW. A 1 GW campus draws about what a large nuclear reactor produces and holds roughly 400–500k Blackwell-class GPUs. Say which basis: IT power is what the chips draw; facility power adds cooling and losses (PUE).

Defined in: W00W01W09merged ×3

H

H100-equivalent

Epoch AI's unit for comparing compute across chip generations.

Defined in: W01

HALEU

High-assay low-enriched uranium (5–20% U-235), needed by many advanced reactors; supply is limited.

Defined in: W03

HBM (high-bandwidth memory)

DRAM dies stacked vertically with through-silicon vias and placed right next to the GPU or accelerator (generations HBM3, 3E, 4, 4E). It is the largest single cost item in an AI chip, the key inference bottleneck and the scarcest part in 2026.

Defined in: W00W05W06W09merged ×4

Heat rate

Fuel (MMBtu) per MWh generated. Lower is more efficient (CCGT ~6.3–6.6; recips/aeros ~8.5–9.5).

Defined in: W03

HPC

High-performance computing, TSMC's platform for AI accelerators, CPUs and networking chips.

Defined in: W06

Hybrid bonding

Direct copper-to-copper and oxide bonding of dies with no solder bumps, allowing <10µm pitch.

Defined in: W06

Hyperscaler

A cloud or platform company operating at global scale with millions of servers: Microsoft, Alphabet/Google, Amazon and Meta, with Oracle usually included for AI (and increasingly xAI). They build and buy at gigawatt scale.

Defined in: W00W01W04W08merged ×4

I

IaaS / PaaS / SaaS

Infrastructure / platform / software as a service: rent raw machines / managed tools / finished apps.

Defined in: W08

IG / HY

Investment grade (BBB- and above) / high yield (BB+ and below; "junk").

Defined in: W02

IMM

Independent market monitor (PJM's is Monitoring Analytics).

Defined in: W03

InfiniBand

Lossless, low-latency networking standard; NVIDIA (Mellanox) is essentially the only vendor.

Defined in: W07

InP

Indium phosphide, the semiconductor used for telecom and datacom lasers.

Defined in: W07

Interconnection / interconnection queue

Interconnection is the utility connection and grid upgrades needed to serve a new load or generator; the queue is the line of projects waiting for grid-impact studies and hookup. (In colocation, "interconnection" also means cross-connects between networks.)

Defined in: W03W04merged ×2

Interposer

A silicon or organic slab with dense wiring that connects dies side by side.

Defined in: W06

IPP

Independent power producer. Owns plants and sells into markets (CEG, VST, TLN, NRG).

Defined in: W03

IRM / reserve margin

Capacity above forecast peak kept for reliability (PJM targets ~20%).

Defined in: W03

IRR / payback

Internal rate of return / payback period: the annualized return on a project, and the time until its cumulative cash flow repays the upfront capex.

Defined in: W08

ISA

Interconnection service agreement.

Defined in: W03

J

Jevons paradox

Cheaper resources leading to greater total consumption, here tokens.

Defined in: W10

K

KV cache

Memory holding attention keys and values during LLM inference; it drives memory demand for agentic AI.

Defined in: W06

Kyber

NVIDIA's 2027 rack architecture for Rubin Ultra (vertical compute blades, 144 packages).

Defined in: W05

L

L6/L10/L11

Board-level / system-level / rack-level integration.

Defined in: W07

Large-load tariff

A special rate class for very large customers, with minimum charges, long terms and collateral.

Defined in: W03

LCOE

Levelized cost of electricity. The lifetime cost per MWh including capital, fuel and O&M.

Defined in: W03

Legacy cash flow

Operating cash from businesses that predate generative AI (search, social ads, retail, Office, non-AI cloud).

Defined in: W11

LPO / LRO

Linear-drive optics (no DSP) / linear-receive optics (half DSP).

Defined in: W07

LPU

Groq's "language processing unit", an SRAM-centric deterministic inference chip.

Defined in: W05

LTA / SCA

Long-term (strategic customer) agreement fixing supply and price over several years, sometimes with prepayments.

Defined in: W06

LTV (loan-to-value)

Debt ÷ collateral value (SoftBank targets below 25%).

Defined in: W02

M

MaaS (model-as-a-service)

Model APIs billed per token (Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, Vertex AI).

Defined in: W08

Mandatory convertible preferred

A preferred share that pays a dividend and must convert into common stock by a set date.

Defined in: W02

Margin loan

A loan secured on shares. It can be called if the share price falls.

Defined in: W02

MCP (Model Context Protocol)

Open standard for connecting models to tools and data.

Defined in: W10

MEP

Mechanical, electrical, plumbing systems.

Defined in: W04

Model lab

A company that trains and sells large AI models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind).

Defined in: W00

MoE (mixture of experts)

An architecture that activates only a subset of parameters per token (e.g., DeepSeek V4-Pro: 1.6T total, 49B active).

Defined in: W09

MW / MWh

Power (rate) vs energy (amount). 1 MW for 1 hour = 1 MWh.

Defined in: W03

$/MW annualised revenue

A neocloud pricing metric: annualised contract revenue divided by the power needed to serve it (CoreWeave's short-dated contracts ~$40M/MW, Sep 2026).

Defined in: W02

N

Neocloud

A GPU-specialist cloud, such as CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe, Nscale, Fluidstack or IREN, that rents accelerators to labs and hyperscalers, often on multi-year contracts.

Defined in: W00W01W02W04W05W08merged ×6

Node (N3, N2)

A process-technology generation; the names are marketing labels.

Defined in: W06

NRC

Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the US nuclear safety regulator that licenses reactors.

Defined in: W03

NRR (net revenue retention)

Revenue from existing customers this year ÷ last year (Fin: 146%).

Defined in: W10

NVL72 / rack

A rack is a cabinet of servers. NVIDIA's NVL72 links 72 GPU packages (GB200, GB300, Vera Rubin) in one NVLink domain so they act as one giant GPU; the rack, not the chip, is now the unit of sale.

Defined in: W00W05W07W08merged ×4

NVLink / NVSwitch / NVLink Fusion

NVIDIA's GPU-to-GPU scale-up interconnect (NVLink) and the switch chip that builds it (NVSwitch). NVLink Fusion licenses it to third-party CPUs and custom XPUs.

Defined in: W05W07merged ×2

O

OCF (operating cash flow)

Cash generated by the business before investment.

Defined in: W01W02merged ×2

OCS

Optical circuit switch (mirrors steer light, no electrical conversion).

Defined in: W07

ODM / OEM

Original design manufacturer, which builds to the customer's design (Foxconn, Quanta, Wiwynn), vs original equipment manufacturer, which sells its own brand (Dell, Supermicro, HPE). Both assemble AI racks.

Defined in: W00W07merged ×2

On-demand / reserved / spot

List price with no commitment / discounted committed capacity / interruptible leftover capacity.

Defined in: W08

Open-weight model

A model whose parameters are published for anyone to download and run (Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral). Not necessarily "open source": licenses vary.

Defined in: W00W09merged ×2

Operating lease

A shorter lease expensed as rent; not capex.

Defined in: W01

Optics / transceiver

Laser-based modules that turn electrical signals into light for fiber links.

Defined in: W00

OSAT

Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (ASE, Amkor).

Defined in: W06

OSFP / QSFP-DD

Pluggable module form factors.

Defined in: W07

Outcome-based pricing

Charging per result (resolution, task) rather than per seat or token.

Defined in: W10

P

PAM4

4-level signaling, 2 bits per symbol.

Defined in: W07

PBC (public benefit corporation)

A for-profit corporate form with a stated public mission (OpenAI Group PBC, Anthropic PBC).

Defined in: W09

PCIe / CXL

Chip-to-chip bus inside servers / memory-coherent extension of PCIe.

Defined in: W07

PDU / RPP

Power distribution unit / remote power panel. Distribute power to rows and racks.

Defined in: W04

PJM

The largest US RTO (13 states plus DC; includes Northern Virginia's "Data Center Alley").

Defined in: W03

PLG (product-led growth)

Users adopt self-serve before any enterprise contract. 27% of AI app spend vs 7% for SaaS.

Defined in: W10

Post-training / RLHF / RLVR

Tuning after pre-training via human feedback (RLHF) or verifiable rewards (RLVR: math and code graders).

Defined in: W09

Powered land

A site with a grid connection or on-site generation already secured. It is the scarce real estate of AI.

Defined in: W00

Powered shell

Building with utility power delivered but without the tenant's MEP fit-out.

Defined in: W04

PPA (power purchase agreement)

A long-term contract to buy electricity from a specific plant. A virtual PPA is a financial contract-for-differences with no physical delivery.

Defined in: W00W03merged ×2

Pre-IPO convertible notes

Debt that converts into shares at the IPO, usually at a discount to the IPO price (e.g. Nscale's $3.36B, Sep 2026).

Defined in: W02

Preleasing

Capacity leased before construction completes.

Defined in: W04

Pre-training

Next-token prediction on massive corpora.

Defined in: W09

Private credit

Loans made by non-bank funds (Blue Owl, Apollo, Blackstone) rather than banks or public bond markets.

Defined in: W00

Profit pool

The operating profit earned at each layer of a value chain. It shows where money is actually kept, and unlike revenue it can be added up across layers.

Defined in: W00W11merged ×2

Prompt caching

Reusing already-processed input tokens at ~10% of the price.

Defined in: W09

PUE (power usage effectiveness)

Total facility power ÷ IT power. Modern liquid-cooled AI halls run about 1.1–1.3 (up to ~1.4).
